1  DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:11474  MFA No. 100315 of 2019
ORAL JUDGMENT

This appeal is by the claimants seeking enhancement of compensation being aggrieved by judgment and award dated 31.07.2018 passed in MVC No.194/2017 on the file of learned II Addl. District and Sessions Judge & Member, MACT-XII, Ballari1.
2.

entities.text: II Addl. District and Sessions Judge & Member, MACT-XII, Ballari1
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Sri. Hanumanthareddy Sahukar, learned counsel for the appellants/claimants submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the notional income of the deceased at Rs.6,500/- per month, as the deceased was working as Tailor and earning Rs.10,000/- per month and was aged about 45 years at the time of the accident.
Hence, he seeks to re-assess the same by allowing the appeal.

3. Per contra, learned counsel Smt. Sharmila M Patil for the respondent/Insurance Company vehemently opposes the appeal and submits that the claimants failed to produce evidence with regard to income of the deceased, hence, the Tribunal has rightly assessed notional income of the deceased at Rs.6,500/- per month, which does not call for enhancement.
She further submits that the award of compensation under all 'Tribunal', for short NC: 2024:KHC-D:11474 heads is just and proper and does not call for modification.
Thus, she seeks dismissal of appeal.
4. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the material on record.
5. It is not in dispute that in a road accident on 28.1.2017, the mother of the claimants sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the same.
The material available on record indicates that the deceased was aged about 45 years.

The claimants have not produced any evidence with regard to income, and in the absence of any evidence on record with regard to income of the deceased, the Tribunal assessed notional income of the deceased at Rs.6,500/- per month.
This Court taking note of notional income chart prepared by KSLSA would re-
assess the notional income of the deceased at Rs.10,250/- per month.
The appellants/claimants are entitled to addition of 25% of the assessed income of the deceased towards loss of future prospects.

Hence, loss of dependency is reckoned as under:
Rs.10,250 + 25% x 12 x 14 x 2/3 = Rs.14,35,000/-
6.

The appellants being children of the deceased are entitled to a sum of Rs.48,000/-
each towards loss of NC: 2024:KHC-D:11474 consortium including 20% escalation,
besides Rs.18,000/-
M.Radha @ Marindi Radha vs Sri.Hanumantha K S/O. Shivappa K on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173075744/
2 towards loss of estate and Rs.18,000/- towards funeral expenses.

In all, the claimants are entitled to modified compensation as under:
Loss of dependency Rs.14,35,000/-
 Loss of consortium Rs. 96,000/-
 Loss of estate & funeral expenses Rs. 36,000/-
 ------------------
 Total Rs.15,67,000/-
 ------------------
7.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER a) Appeal stands partly allowed.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified holding that the claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.15,67,000/- as against Rs.9,40,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
c) The enhanced compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
d) The respondent/insurer shall deposit the enhanced compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
e) Apportionment, deposit and disbursement shall be made as per award of the Tribunal.

NC: 2024:KHC-D:11474 f) Draw modified award accordingly.
g) No costs.

Sd/-
(VIJAYKUMAR A.PATIL) JUDGE JTR/ct-an M.Radha @ Marindi Radha vs Sri.Hanumantha K S/O. Shivappa K on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173075744/
